## What does commercial cleaning cost in Newcastle?

There is no reliable single price for an undefined cleaning service. Floor area, how the workplace is used, the task schedule, access, visit frequency and periodic work all affect the proposal. A square-metre or hourly rate can be a starting point, but it cannot tell you whether two offers cover the same job.

This guide helps you compare the full commitment before choosing a provider. It does not publish a YOS rate card or claim an average Newcastle market price. YOS provides [commercial cleaning in Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie](/cleaning), with a site inspection informing the written proposal.

## Start with the workload, not just square metres

Two offices of the same size can have very different cleaning needs. One might be occupied twice a week with a small kitchen; the other may host clients daily and have several heavily used amenities. A floor-area price hides those differences unless the scope explains them.

Prepare these details for the site inspection:

- The address, approximate area and areas you occupy versus common property.
- Attendance patterns, visitor use and busy days.
- Kitchens, washrooms, meeting rooms and waste points.
- Floor materials, accessible surfaces and restricted areas.
- The proposed service window and building-access requirements.
- Existing condition and any initial detail work needed.
- Routine tasks, periodic tasks and work requiring a separate provider or quote.

Do not put alarm codes, passwords or private staff information in a general quote brief. Agree a secure access handover separately.

## Five ways a quoted price can mislead you

**A price per visit needs a visit count.** Ask how many visits the annual allowance includes, including shutdowns and public holidays. Do not assume every provider has priced the same calendar.

**An hourly price needs a scope and labour assumption.** Clarify whether the quoted hours are total labour hours or elapsed time, what tasks they cover and whether the price is a budget estimate or a fixed commitment. Two people attending for one hour is different from one total labour hour.

**A square-metre price needs an area definition.** Does the area include storage, meeting rooms, amenities or shared corridors? Who measured it? Compare the same included areas and task schedule.

**A monthly price needs an inclusion list.** Regular visits, periodic work, consumables and initial cleaning may sit in different lines. Ask whether the monthly amount is fixed or an average across the year.

**A low headline price may leave decisions open.** An unpriced item is not automatically included or free. Request a revised written proposal for material clarifications.

## A worked annual comparison

The figures below are invented solely to show the arithmetic. They are not YOS prices, Newcastle market benchmarks or estimates for your office. Both hypothetical proposals use 156 routine visits a year, and all amounts are on the same ex-GST basis.

| Cost component | Hypothetical proposal A | Hypothetical proposal B |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Routine visits | 156 × $110 = $17,160 | 156 × $125 = $19,500 |
| Periodic detail work | 4 × $450 = $1,800 | Included at the same defined scope |
| Consumables allowance | $1,200 | $1,200 |
| Total recurring annual allowance | $20,160 | $20,700 |
| Effective cost per routine visit, with these allowances spread across it | $129.23 | $132.69 |

The headline difference is $15 per visit. Once those stated allowances are included, the recurring annual difference is $540. That calculation still does not decide which proposal is better: you must compare the actual tasks, periodic scope, management, access and terms.

Now suppose A also requires a separately quoted $600 initial clean and B includes the equivalent initial scope. The first-year totals become $20,760 and $20,700. In this invented example, the first-year order reverses. Recurring and first-year costs answer different questions.

Keep GST treatment consistent and have unclear commercial terms explained before committing. Actual visit counts, allowances and tax treatment must come from your proposals, not this example.

## Use this quote-comparison worksheet

Copy the table into your procurement notes or use our existing [Workplace Cleaning Brief & Comparison Checklist (PDF)](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf). The pack is free to read without email registration.

| Record for each proposal | What to confirm |
| --- | --- |
| Scope revision and site | Same areas, tasks and exclusions |
| Routine visits | Number, timing, closures and public-holiday treatment |
| Periodic work | Exact tasks, cycles and included or separate price |
| Initial work | Condition assessment and any one-off charge |
| Supplies and consumables | Supplier, allowance, replenishment and variation basis |
| Access | Inductions, service window and failed-access arrangements |
| Management | Named contact, cover arrangements and quality reviews |
| Price basis | GST, fixed versus estimated amounts and validity |
| Changes and exit | Approval process, notice, renewal and cancellation provisions |

Compare one representative year of recurring costs, then show commencement costs separately. Do not assume a universal notice period: review your actual agreement and seek advice where needed.

## What to ask before accepting a cleaning quote

1. Can we walk the premises together and confirm the scope revision?
2. Which tasks happen each visit, periodically, separately or not at all?
3. Which assumptions could change the price?
4. What evidence of relevant experience and current insurance can you provide?
5. Who manages the service and how are missed tasks recorded and followed up?
6. What happens when staffing, attendance, access or our layout changes?
7. Can you put the clarifications and agreed price basis in the final proposal?

These questions are checks to make with a provider, not claims that every provider holds the same credentials or offers identical terms. Ordinary office cleaning should not be assumed to cover specialist clinical, hazardous-material or food-production requirements.

## Make the price useful after commencement

Keep the final proposal with its task schedule. At the first agreed review, compare what has actually happened with the included work. A missed included task needs follow-up; a new requirement may need a scope change. Record the difference before assuming an extra visit will solve it.

For a fuller briefing method, use our [Newcastle office cleaning guide](/blog/commercial-cleaning-newcastle-what-to-expect). If the workplace has changed, read [how to review a busier office's cleaning scope](/blog/commercial-cleaning-scope-busier-office).
